title: Diffusivity in Dissipative Quantum Transport from an Exactly Solvable Krylov Chain
abstract: The computation of transport coefficients in interacting quantum many-body systems is rarely analytically accessible. Here, we develop a new Krylov-space mechanism that makes the leading density dependent correction to Green-Kubo diffusivity \emph{exactly} calculable in the strong-dissipation regime of a one-dimensional noisy spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ XXZ chain. This is done by showing that the density-polarization-dressed bond coherence generates a Krylov subspace where repeated action of the dissipator closes exactly on an explicitly identifiable operator family. Within this subspace, the dissipative dynamics is then mapped onto a self-similar semi-infinite chain with a boundary defect. Surprisingly, \emph{all} Lanczos coefficients of the Krylov chain and its boundary Green's function can be determined exactly. The latter then determines the exact leading density-dependent correction to the diffusivity. Finally, we calculate analytically the full boundary-to-bulk Green's function and find that it decays exponentially along the emergent Krylov chain.
summary: This work develops a novel Krylov-space mechanism to exactly calculate the leading interaction correction to the diffusivity in a dissipative quantum spin chain. By mapping the dynamics onto a solvable semi-infinite Krylov chain, the authors derive a closed-form, microscopic expression for the transport coefficient in the strong-dissipation regime. This provides a powerful analytical tool for understanding quantum transport in open many-body systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the analytically challenging computation of transport coefficients, specifically the leading density-dependent correction to the diffusivity, in interacting quantum many-body systems.
main_result: The authors analytically determine this correction by mapping the dissipative dynamics onto a self-similar semi-infinite Krylov chain, yielding a closed-form expression for the diffusivity.
method: The core method involves developing a novel Krylov-space mechanism applied to the Green-Kubo formula within the strong-dissipation regime, allowing for the exact solution of the resulting operator hierarchy.
model_or_system: The system studied is a one-dimensional spin-1/2 XXZ chain undergoing Lindbladian evolution due to symmetric incoherent nearest-neighbor spin exchange. The model is mapped onto an interacting spinless-fermion chain.
key_observables: Diffusivity (D), the interaction-dependent correction to diffusivity ($D_{GK}$), and the boundary Green's function ($G_{m1}$).
important_parameters: Strong-dissipation regime ($\gamma \gg |J|, |U|$), hopping amplitude ($J$), interaction strength ($U$), and dissipation rate ($\gamma$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system supports only a diffusive mode and relies on the strong-dissipation limit for the perturbative expansion.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general framework using the Mori-Zwanzig formalism and the Green-Kubo formula. It then focuses on the strong-dissipation limit, where the problem is mapped onto an emergent Krylov chain structure. The solvability of this chain allows for the exact determination of the boundary Green's function, which yields the final result for $D_{GK}$.
why_interesting: The rigorous application of Krylov subspace techniques to solve non-equilibrium quantum dynamics in the strong-dissipation limit provides a powerful, exact analytical tool for calculating transport properties in open quantum systems.
